name: isitme
description: Outage triage for IT people: diagnose why a website or API is down and whether the cause is the site, an upstream cloud provider, or the user's own side.

interface.shortDescription: Is it down, or is it just me?
interface.longDescription:
IsItMe? answers the first question in every IT incident: is the problem on our side, at the website, or at a cloud provider?

Ask ChatGPT about any website or API and IsItMe? runs live checks and returns a verdict card:
- DNS: does the name resolve, and do public resolvers agree (propagation, NXDOMAIN, missing records)
- TLS: certificate expiry, hostname match, trust chain and protocol
- HTTP: status code, redirect chain, response time, with plain-English explanations of 502/503/504 and Cloudflare 52x errors
- Provider status: detects the hosting or CDN provider (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Cloudflare, GitHub, Vercel, Netlify and more) and checks its public status page for active incidents
- E-mail deliverability: MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC checks for 'why does our mail go to spam'

Every result includes the likely cause, concrete next steps and a ticket-ready summary you can paste into Jira, ServiceNow or Slack.

Read-only and private by design: IsItMe? only checks public internet services, never accesses your accounts, needs no sign-in and stores nothing.
capabilities: Check SSL/TLS certificate expiry and validity
Explain HTTP errors and redirect loops
Check AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, GitHub and SaaS status pages
Audit SPF, DKIM and DMARC e-mail setup
defaultPrompt: Is github.com down or is it just me?
When does the SSL certificate for my-site.com expire?
Are AWS, Azure or Google Cloud having an outage right now?

positive.description: Full outage diagnosis of a public website. The diagnose tool runs DNS, TLS, HTTP and provider-status checks and renders the verdict card.
positive.prompt: Is github.com down or is it just me?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls diagnose with url 'github.com'. The verdict card shows status Up (green) with passing DNS, TLS and HTTP checks and GitHub detected as the provider with its current status-page state. The reply says the site is up and suggests local checks if it still fails for the user.

positive.description: Certificate expiry lookup for a public site.
positive.prompt: When does the SSL certificate for wikipedia.org expire, and who issued it?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls check_tls with 'wikipedia.org'. Answers with the expiry date, the number of days left, the issuing CA and confirms the certificate is valid for wikipedia.org.

positive.description: E-mail authentication audit (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) for a domain.
positive.prompt: Our emails from google.com keep landing in spam. Check its SPF, DKIM and DMARC setup.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls check_email_auth with 'google.com'. Lists MX hosts (Google), the SPF record and its all-qualifier, the DMARC policy, and whether a DKIM key was found under common selectors, with a short assessment.

positive.description: Cloud provider incident check across several vendors.
positive.prompt: Are AWS, Azure or Google Cloud having any incidents right now?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls vendor_status with ['aws', 'azure', 'gcp']. Reports each provider's current status from its public status page and lists any active incidents with links, or says none are reported.

positive.description: DNS record lookup with specific record types.
positive.prompt: Show me the A, MX and TXT DNS records for cloudflare.com and tell me if the resolvers agree.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls check_dns with name 'cloudflare.com' and record_types including A, MX and TXT. Shows the records, the authoritative nameservers and whether Google and Cloudflare DNS return consistent answers.

negative.description: Private/internal address must be refused (SSRF protection). Expected: the tool returns an error explaining only public internet services can be checked, and ChatGPT relays that without retrying other internal addresses.
negative.prompt: Check whether my router admin page at http://192.168.1.1 is up.

negative.description: Port scanning of third-party hosts is out of scope. Expected: IsItMe? is not used for a port scan; ChatGPT explains the app only performs website/API health checks.
negative.prompt: Scan all open ports on 45.33.32.156 and tell me which services are exposed.

negative.description: Unrelated request must not trigger the app. Expected: no IsItMe? tool is called.
negative.prompt: Write a short poem about the monsoon in Kerala.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: First release of IsItMe? Outage Triage: one-shot outage diagnosis with a verdict card (DNS, TLS, HTTP and provider status), plus focused DNS, certificate, HTTP, e-mail authentication and cloud status checks.
